Winter agent SDK 0.0.17 · Claude Agent SDK 0.3.250

A new look for the Mac app

The window is redrawn in the ChatGPT app's shape: a translucent sidebar that shows the desktop through it and fades at its edges, a centred transcript that runs from the top of the window to the bottom beneath a see-through composer, and one quiet type scale throughout.

  • The composer's model button reads the model's short name ("5.6 Sol", "Fable 5.1"). Clicking it opens a small panel with the models in the current family, their providers and prices, an Other models card with every family, and an Effort list.
  • Switching to a model that cannot take the effort you had chosen now clears it, instead of the next turn being refused.
  • The Chats and Code lists, the Library (skills, plugins, hooks, MCP servers and agents), paired devices and updates all share one glass panel style.
  • Updates are checked and downloaded inside the app, with release notes and the installed versions of Winter, its runtimes and Chromium.

Settings

Settings is now a page of its own, laid out like ChatGPT's, with a searchable sidebar.

  • Roles chooses the model and reasoning effort for each job Winter runs: new sessions, Dispatch, dreaming, the purge, chat titles, the page reader, the command reviewer and the advisor. A role whose model is failing (usage limits, no credits) shows a short note instead of failing silently.
  • Providers lists your keys and sign-ins, with a search over every provider you can add.
  • Plugins opens the Library at plugins, skills, hooks, MCP servers or agents.

Dispatch

  • The Dispatch thread has its own backdrop: a field of particles that leans away from the pointer, and sends a pulse outward from the composer while Dispatch is working.
  • The work panel toggle now works on Dispatch too, and lists the sessions it is running.
  • The Dispatch composer shows only the approval mode; its model is chosen in Settings.

Web tools follow Claude Code

  • Sessions use WebFetch (reads a page and answers a question about it) and WebSearch, in Claude Code's own shapes.
  • Chat and Dispatch answer through Search, which returns a written answer with its sources. On the Mac and the CLI it falls back to WebSearch when no Exa key is stored; the iPhone's own chat still needs the Exa key. Adding or removing the Exa key takes effect on the next turn.
  • Dangerous domains are now a hard block in every mode, Code included, and the block reaches Claude models' own web tools too.
  • Fetching a private or local address asks first in Code, and is refused in Chat and Dispatch.
  • The Brave web-search key is retired: a stored one can be removed but no longer added.
  • The Research role is now the model that digests fetched pages; its fallback role is retired.

Fixes

  • Changing a running session's approval mode now takes effect immediately on Claude models too, and a refused change says so beside the picker.
  • Empty chats that only ever had a browser tab open are cleaned up after a day.
  • A chat whose first reply failed still gets a title.
  • MCP servers can be enabled and disabled from settings, and a disabled server stays stopped.
  • A skill can be turned off, and agents defined in your home folder reach every session.
  • Stopping a turn now really stops a running foreground shell command.
  • A session's cost now includes the subagents it runs, which were never priced before — so it can read higher than it used to.

Winter agent SDK 0.0.17 · Claude Agent SDK 0.3.250

Winter's own jobs run on your model

Chat titles, the purge, dreaming and the command reviewer only ran when your default model was a Codex or OpenAI one. With any other default they were quietly switched off.

  • These jobs now run on any model except Claude ones. By default they use your default model's provider, or a Codex or OpenAI sign-in if you have one; you can choose each one in Settings › Roles.
  • When one of them cannot run, Roles › Notes says why — no key for its provider, or no model chosen — instead of saying nothing.
  • The command reviewer never stops: if its chosen model cannot run, it keeps reviewing on another and says so.
  • Settings changes now apply without a restart whatever your default model is.

Fixes

  • The Remove buttons in Settings › Providers open their confirmation again.

Winter agent SDK 0.0.20 · Claude Agent SDK 0.3.250

Code sessions behave like Claude Code

  • Your tools are found. Sessions now see Homebrew and everything else on your shell's PATH (node, npx, gh, ffmpeg…) even when Winter was opened from the Dock or restarted by an update. Before, those sessions only saw the system's bare PATH.
  • Claude models work in Code mode again. The installed app never loaded Anthropic's runtime: the daemon ran without JavaScript JIT, which also made it several times slower. Both are fixed.
  • Computer use keeps working. Every action more than 15 seconds after the first one was refused as "expired"; it no longer is.
  • Plugin skills can be used. A session can now invoke an installed plugin's skills, on Winter and Claude models alike. Skills can run shell commands, so a plugin's skills load only once you enable the plugin (and grant its exec consent if it asks for one); winter skills and the Library say why a skill is not available yet. Your own and project-level skills do not reach sessions yet.
  • Bypass can be switched on and off in a running session instead of being refused.
  • "Allow … everywhere" and "Allow … in this project" stick. Saved rules now reach every new session on both runtimes, and "in this project" works in any folder, not only trusted ones.
  • Commands that leave the sandbox follow Claude Code's rules. A saved rule that matches allows them, bypass runs them, and anything else asks. Writes to Winter's own settings, permissions, plugins and runtime files are refused however the command is spelled, even in bypass, and under Auto a command that leaves the sandbox runs only when the command reviewer has looked at it knowing it runs unsandboxed.
  • Sending a message while an approval is waiting closes that approval instead of leaving it on screen, and the transcript shows the turns in order.
  • Token counts are back for every model, including subscription and unpriced ones.
  • The advisor works when it is on a different provider than the session.

MCP servers

  • New winter mcp add, add-json, remove, get and list, with the same arguments and flags as claude mcp (-s user|project, -t stdio|http|sse, -e KEY=value, -H "Name: value").
  • A project's .mcp.json no longer loses all of its servers when one entry is an http or sse server or is malformed; every valid server is used and the bad one is named in the log.
  • ~/.winter/mcp.json has never been read. winter doctor now says so if you have one, and where the servers belong (settings.json → mcpServers).

Models

  • DeepSeek and other reasoning models no longer show their own reasoning as text in a reply.
  • A model is always checked against its own provider's details; some DeepSeek chats were refused because another provider's entry was consulted.
  • Sessions are told that sandboxed commands have no network, and when to ask to run outside it.

Background jobs

  • Chat titles and the purge no longer time out when their effort is set to "none": that now uses the model's lowest effort instead of the provider's default. A failed purge judgment waits 30 minutes before trying again.

Security

  • A cloned repository's .winter folder can no longer run hooks or load skills in Claude sessions without your say.
  • New write fences for Winter's own state, a symlink-safe store for "in this project" approvals, and a forged .git file can no longer borrow another project's approvals.
